unit_label: Section 8: Involutionsbasis der Integritätsbereiche J_{n rho} aus Polynomen
translation_source_policy: Translated directly from the audited German source slice. English control was used only as a sanity witness for older divisibility, involution-form, and integral-domain vocabulary; this unit was not edited from another target-language draft.

technical_exclusions.disposition: Section 9 and later Paper 06 content; not included in this checkpoint.

segment_summaries.content: Section heading: involution basis for polynomial integral domains.
segment_summaries.choices: Keeps the Section 5 involution-basis lane and the Section 7 integral-domain lane; Interslavic uses `involucijska baza integralnyh oblastij iz polinomov`.

segment_summaries.content: Restricts the following paragraphs to systems whose elements are whole rational functions, explicitly polynomials, and announces divisibility notions.
segment_summaries.choices: `ganze rationale Funktionen (Polynome)` is rendered as whole rational functions, that is, polynomials, preserving Noether's historical wording while making the modern reading explicit.

segment_summaries.content: Defines common divisor inside J_{n rho}: not only L but also the two quotients must belong to the domain.
segment_summaries.choices: Common divisor is `спільний дільник` / `общий делитель` / `obči dělitelj`; the domain-internal condition is kept explicit.

segment_summaries.content: Defines relatively prime inside J_{n rho}.
segment_summaries.choices: Uses standard relatively-prime vocabulary in Ukrainian/Russian and transparent Interslavic `vzajemno prosty`.

segment_summaries.content: Every function in the smallest containing field has a quotient presentation by relatively prime J-polynomials; several functions can be put over a least common denominator in J.
segment_summaries.choices: The colon quotient notation is preserved; `kleinster gemeinsamer Nenner` becomes least/smallest common denominator.

segment_summaries.content: The quotient presentation need not be unique because unique factorization into irreducibles may fail inside J.
segment_summaries.choices: Modern algebra register uses unique factorization while preserving Noether's `irreduzible Funktionen` wording as irreducible functions rather than flattening to factors.

segment_summaries.content: Transfers the field involution form to a polynomial integral domain by multiplying by a least common denominator, producing a domain involution form and basis with relatively prime coefficients.
segment_summaries.choices: The long display was explicitly aligned in TeX after render audit to prevent formula walk-off.

segment_summaries.content: Every involution basis of J is also a rational basis; introduces the mapping domain J* and its smallest containing field.
segment_summaries.choices: `Abbildungsbereich` continues as mapping domain / `oblast odobraženja`, not image set only.

segment_summaries.content: Uses Section 5: coefficients of Phi* are elementary symmetric functions of conjugate rows; any polynomial in K* is a whole rational combination of them. The domain involution form then gives denominator quotients.
segment_summaries.choices: Reuses `redy veličin`, `elementarne simetrične funkcije`, and `cěla racionalna kombinacija`; these are important for later Section 14 symmetry language.

segment_summaries.content: By the transfer principle, Theorem VI: every polynomial integral domain has a distinguished rational basis, the involution basis, whose rational representations use only powers of one fixed denominator function.
segment_summaries.choices: The fixed function is glossed as the highest coefficient of the corresponding involution form; theorem label VI remains Roman in both Interslavic scripts.

cyrillic_manual_normalizations.correction: No manual correction required; the transliterator protected `VI` as a Roman theorem label.
cyrillic_manual_normalizations.rationale: Roman theorem numbers remain Roman across script variants.

review_flags: `Integritätsbereich aus Polynomen` remains `integralna oblast iz polinomov` in Interslavic; authority review may prefer a more Slavic calque for `integralna` but this matches previous Paper 06 sections.
`děliteljnost`, `obči dělitelj`, and `vzajemno prosty` are transparent and pan-Slavic, but final authority review should check whether `děliteljnost` or `dělimost` is preferred.
`najmenši obči imenovatelj` is used for least common denominator; check consistency with any later fixed-denominator terminology in Sections 10--12.
`redy veličin` is intentionally reused from Section 5; this phrase needs cumulative Interslavic review because it is semantically accurate but not a high-frequency modern term.
